title: Pre-Check and Double-Check (TOCTOU and Redundancy)
pattern: An explicit condition check (like checking if a file or directory exists) is performed immediately before executing an operation that naturally returns a failure variant if the check fails.
why_bad: It introduces a Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) race condition—the file could be deleted between the existence check and the open call. Additionally, it writes redundant error-handling blocks because the standard library function already performs and returns this check safely.
detection: The invocation of a path existence check or handle-validity check immediately preceding an I/O operation on that same target path/handle.
fix: Eliminate the pre-check. Execute the operation directly and handle the resulting `Result` or error variant, ensuring atomic safety.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 8.1 ("Protecting Your Program from Invalid Inputs") / Section 8.3 ("Error-Handling Techniques").
